summary: One resolution point, two entrances, as contracted: hook commands route through `forge hook <name>` with the interpreter chain living only in the entrypoint, double exit-2 fail-closed (inner and outer) so a dead resolver blocks rather than vanishes; forge.cmd delegates to the same point; .gitattributes pins forge eol=lf (the worker's CRLF catch - the launcher itself was a fail-open vector); doctor executes all eight registered hooks with benign payloads and reds by name; the windows-latest job is harness-gated. Cross-session provenance recorded honestly: the diff is joint work under the human's pen ruling, decision 0038 (portable-fail-closed-hooks) was drafted in-flight by the other session and needs acceptance.

non_blocking_findings.summary: A decision record entered via the parallel session rather than this plan's Decisions section (which said none needed); content is sound and rides for human acceptance - governance caught up at review rather than at authoring.
A second stale running entry (the other session's 4h verifying worker) persists in the registry; liveness detection remains follow-up material from FORGE-ROLE-1's review.

residual_risks: Windows behavior is proven by the CI job from this PR onward; real client machines vary beyond the runner image - doctor's red rows are the client-side truth.
